amendments.rule: Rule 55's correlative clause is not peculiar to a crasis. Where a **separate** `καί` answers a preceding comparative `καθώς`, `καθάπερ` or `ὡς`, that `καί` takes the whole English correlative — *so* or *even so* — and the comparative adverb keeps only *as* or *even as*. `καθὼς … καὶ ὑμεῖς` → *as … so ye* gives *so* to the conjunction at JHN.6.57 and JHN.13.33, as `ὡς … καὶ` → *As … so* does at GAL.1.9 and 2CO.13.2, and as `καθὼς ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν` → *as he is, even so are we* does at 1JN.4.17. Rule 55 already gives the reason and it does not depend on the crasis: the comparative adverb has its own English word already, and the correlative is what the `καί` writes. The corpus confirms it from the other side, `καθώς` being rendered *even as*, *as* or *according as* in all sixty-nine of its units and never taking *so*. Rule 17 heads such a unit on ***so***, the word that realizes the correlative; a supplied *even* is an intensifying helper on it under rules 7 and 11, exactly as it is where `οὕτως` takes *even so* at JHN.3.14, JHN.5.21, JHN.5.26 and JHN.14.31 and where `ναί` does at REV.1.7. So do not head such a unit on *even* merely because *even* is the more direct gloss of `καί`: that gloss is what a bare *even* answers to where no *so* competes, as at 2CO.11.12 and EPH.2.3, and it does not carry where the ASV writes the correlative out. Where the ASV writes **no** correlative and renders the comparative together with its answering `καί` by a bare *even as*, that is exactly where the gloss does carry: the `καί` is `aligned` to *even* and headed on it, and the comparative keeps a bare *as* as its own unit, as `καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς` → *even as we* does at 2CO.11.12, `ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί` → *even as the rest* at EPH.2.3, and `καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο` → *even as it came to pass* at 1TH.3.4. Do not give *even as* whole to the comparative and leave the `καί` `unrepresented`: rule 65's English-side test empties an intensifying `καί` only where the ASV writes no word for it, and a written *even* is such a word. Where the ASV writes a word of the particle's **own** — ***also*** — the bare-*even* arm does not apply. That word is the `καί`'s under rule 65, and the comparative keeps *even as* whole as its own unit headed on *as*, as `καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς` → *even as we also* does at 1TH.3.6 and 1TH.3.12. Rule 76's availability test is what forces this — a particle the ASV has already spent on *also* is not a word the supplied *even* can belong to — and rule 100 settles the identical division for `οὕτως … καί` → *even so … also* unanimously across thirteen units, the adverb keeping the whole correlative and the particle taking only *also*. So do not stretch the `καί` discontinuously over *even … also*, and do not read a written *also* as licence to strip *even* from the comparative. A comparative with **no** answering `καί` is the contrast and keeps *even as* whole under rules 7 and 11, no other source token standing to claim the supplied *even*, so a chapter writing both — `καθώς` alone as *even as* and `καθὼς καί` as *even* plus *as* — is following rule 24's habit and not two analyses. The test is not merely whether a `καί` stands in the construction but which English word the ASV wrote for it: a written *so* is the correlative arm and is the `καί`'s, a written *also* is the particle's and leaves *even as* whole on the comparative, a bare *even as* with no other word for the particle splits into the `καί`'s *even* and the comparative's *as*, and no answering `καί` at all leaves *even as* whole on the comparative. Never decide it from how the same comparative was rendered where a different word, or none, stood.
amendments.why: Rule 82 enumerates only two arms for an answering καί — a written correlative *so*, and a bare *even as* whose *even* is the particle's — and closes with a test naming only whether a καί stands in the construction. 1TH.3.6 and 3:12 met the third arm: the ASV writes *also* for the particle and *even as* for the comparative. Read as it stands, rule 82 would push a pass either to give the particle a discontinuous *even … also*, or to strip *even* off the comparative and leave the written *also* nowhere rule 65 permits. The amendment adds that arm and rewrites the closing test as which English word the ASV wrote rather than whether a καί stands, keeping the existing sentences and their citations intact. The basis is rule 100, which already settles the identical division for οὕτως … καί → *even so … also* across thirteen unanimous corpus units, together with rule 65's English-side test and rule 76's availability principle; the καί corpus rows show *also* in 415 units and contradict nothing here. `καθάπερ` is added to the opening enumeration because both units carrying this arm are καθάπερ and the rule was being applied to it already; the sixty-nine-unit claim stays scoped to καθώς, as before.

conventions: Elliptical comparative clauses: the chapter has two and analyses them differently because the Greek differs, not the English. 3:12's καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς has a prepositional predicate, so the supplied lexical do rides with εἰς under rule 62, headed on the prepositional word. 3:6's καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς has no preposition, and the supplied to see repeats an ἰδεῖν already spent earlier in the same verse, so it is added under rules 5 and 103. Rule 62's reading of rule 56 does not carry a supplied lexical verb onto the subject pronoun where rule 103 has already spent the token that would license it: rule 7's list does not include a full lexical verb, so the absence of a competitor licenses no fold.

Comparative with an answering καί: the ASV's own wording decides the arm, and both arms stand in this chapter under one analysis. Where the ASV writes also for the particle (3:6, 3:12 καθάπερ καί), also is the καί's under rule 65 and the comparative keeps even as whole, headed on as. Where it writes no word of the particle's own (3:4 καθὼς καί → even as it came to pass), the particle takes even and the comparative a bare as, as rule 82's bare-even arm and 2CO.11.12 have it. Do not stretch a καί discontinuously over even … also.

report: Read all 27 candidate lemma groups and the full dump end to end. No cross-verse split was found: every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently in a different context, and the source licenses each difference.

Checked closely and cleared: the four εἰς τό + infinitive units (3:2 to, 3:5 that, 3:10 that, 3:13 to the end) are one analysis under rules 24 and 61, the preposition taking the clause-introducer and the article unrepresented every time; the three preverb particles (behind 3:1, beforehand 3:4, again 3:9) all ride inside their verb's own unit under rule 106; the three supplied when's on participles (3:1, 3:5, 3:6) all fold under rule 86; πάσῃ/πάντας/πάντων all take a bare all; ὁ κύριος gives the determiner to the article at 3:11 and 3:12 while the anarthrous κυρίῳ at 3:8 takes a supplied the as a rule 51 helper on the noun.

The table is blind to added units, so the two candidates it cannot show were read from the dump. (a) 3:6's supplied to see is added while 3:12's supplied do folds onto εἰς: licensed, because 3:12's elliptical comparative clause has a prepositional predicate (rule 62) and 3:6's has none while its ἰδεῖν is already spent earlier in the verse (rule 103). (b) 3:2's supplied resumptive you folds onto παρακαλέσαι while 3:6's repeated lexical verb is added: that is rule 103's own pronoun-versus-verb contrast, not a split.

The comparative with an answering καί is analysed two ways — 3:4 gives even to the particle and a bare as to καθώς, 3:6 and 3:12 give also to the particle and even as whole to καθάπερ — and the difference is licensed by the ASV writing also in the latter two. Rule 82 does not name that arm and its closing test would push a pass the other way, so the qualification is returned as an amendment to rule 82.

One correction, within a verse rather than across verses: 1TH.3.10 s014/s015. The unit gave that which to the article and only is lacking to ὑστερήματα, citing rule 22; but ὑστερήματα is an expressed head noun, so rule 31's test makes the article attributive and rule 92 governs, keeping the relativizer and the copula together on the noun and leaving the article only the antecedent the ASV wrote. The unit had already put the copula on the noun, so the relativizer was stranded on the wrong side of its own analysis. Patch attached; the rest of the verse is unchanged.

BSB: all three disagreements are articles — 3:3's articular-infinitive τό, 3:6's second-conjunct τήν before ἀγάπην, 3:9's τοῦ displaced by our. Each is a documented convention difference (rules 61, 23, 20) and none is a genuine error. Nothing was changed to close them; the 3:10 patch touches no BSB-compared token, both articles there being aligned in the accepted file.
